title: CUDA error
body: When I use whisper.cpp compiled with CUDA, the large-v3 model loads on my NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Ti SUPER and begins transcribing, but after the first few lines it crashes with `CUDA error: invalid argument` in `ggml_backend_cuda_graph_compute` at `cudaGraphKernelNodeSetParams`. Running with `-ng` to disable the GPU works at the expected CPU speed.

symptoms_visible: The CUDA build loads the large-v3 model and transcribes the first few lines, then aborts with `CUDA error: invalid argument` in `ggml_backend_cuda_graph_compute` at `cudaGraphKernelNodeSetParams`.
The same model and audio work at the expected CPU speed when I use `-ng`.
N0.label: N0 CUDA transcription crash reported

symptoms_visible: The CUDA run still stops after the first seconds with the same invalid-argument error, while `-ng` continues to work.
N1.label: N1 platform versions collected

symptoms_visible: The same CUDA invalid-argument crash also occurs on another Ubuntu GPU setup.
On that setup, a run with `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` no longer produces the error.
N2.label: N2 runtime toggle isolates failing path

symptoms_visible: After rebuilding the corrected current master, whisper.cpp compiles and starts transcribing again, but after the first seconds it still aborts with `CUDA error: invalid argument` in `ggml_backend_cuda_graph_compute`.
N3_x.label: N3_x generic update and rebuild aftermath

symptoms_visible: After rebuilding with the CUDA-graphs build definition removed, GPU transcription works normally and the invalid-argument error is gone.
N_terminal.label: terminal CUDA transcription verified working

question_patterns: Which Linux distribution and kernel version are you using?
Can you paste the output of `uname -a` and identify the Linux release?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I am using Ubuntu Linux 24.04. `uname -a` reports Linux 6.8.0-35-generic on x86_64.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I am running Windows rather than Linux, and the error comes from a different CUDA call.
I am using another Ubuntu 24.04 kernel from the same 6.8 series.

question_patterns: Which CUDA toolkit version are you compiling with?
Can you paste the output of `nvcc --version`?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: `nvcc --version` reports CUDA compilation tools release 12.0, V12.0.140.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: There is no CUDA toolkit installed and this binary was not compiled with CUDA support.
The toolkit is CUDA 12.1 rather than 12.0, with the same runtime error.

edges.comment: Reporter evidence from c6 and c9. The NVIDIA driver update from 535 to 550 was volunteered with uncertainty and is not treated as the cause.

question_patterns: Can this be reproduced on another CUDA-enabled Ubuntu setup?
Does another affected environment produce the same failing CUDA call?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I can reproduce what appears to be the same failure on Ubuntu 22.04 in a GPU instance built with the repository's Dockerfile: transcription begins, then the run aborts from the CUDA graph compute path.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The other GPU setup completes the same audio without any CUDA error.

question_patterns: Did changing any runtime environment setting alter the result?
Can you report whether any one-run environment toggle changes the crash?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Setting the environment variable `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS` to `1` makes the error go away for me.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same invalid-argument error occurs with `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1`.
The run also succeeds when I set the variable inline for only that command.

edges.comment: c3 and c5 came from a second affected user and are folded into the simulated user side. The raw observations are the matching CUDA-path crash and that the environment-variable run has no error; the conclusion that CUDA graphs are the root cause remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Update to the current master, clean the existing build artifacts, and rebuild from scratch as a generic stale-build remedy.
solution.concrete_example: Pull or download the current master, remove the old build output, and rebuild from a fresh source directory before retrying the CUDA transcription.

edges.comment: c2 and c7-c14, reporter's system. The intervening compile failure was a separate Makefile-update problem and is not promoted into the opening runtime issue's causal chain. After a fresh build on the corrected current source compiled successfully, the original CUDA graph runtime error remained, so a generic update/clean rebuild alone is falsified.

solution.intent: Stop enabling CUDA graphs in whisper.cpp builds, update the Makefile or build scripts so `GGML_CUDA_USE_GRAPHS` is not defined, rebuild, and have the reporter verify GPU transcription on the resulting build.
solution.concrete_example: Remove `GGML_CUDA_USE_GRAPHS` from the whisper.cpp Makefile/build configuration, rebuild the CUDA binary, and rerun the same large-v3 transcription. `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` can be used as a temporary runtime workaround while obtaining the corrected build.
solution.inference_hint: The user supplied the stack location, the Makefile definition, and the raw result that `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` avoids the error. The maintainer conclusion is that the finicky CUDA graph implementation should not be enabled outside llama.cpp and therefore must be removed from whisper.cpp's build scripts.

edges.comment: Final diagnosis from c4/c13 and resolution from c15-c16. The reporter rebuilt after the build-script correction and confirmed that it works and the error is gone.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: whisper.cpp's Makefile/build configuration enabled the CUDA graph path even though that implementation should not be used outside llama.cpp, leading to the invalid-argument failure in CUDA graph node parameter updates.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: the stack fails in `ggml_backend_cuda_graph_compute`, the build defines `GGML_CUDA_USE_GRAPHS`, and a run with `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1` avoids the error.
The durable fix must remove or stop defining `GGML_CUDA_USE_GRAPHS` in whisper.cpp's build scripts and rebuild; the environment variable may be offered only as a temporary workaround.
Must not treat switching permanently to CPU with `-ng`, changing NVIDIA drivers, or merely cleaning and rebuilding the same graph-enabled source as the final fix.
Must ask the reporter to verify the same GPU transcription on a build containing the build-script correction before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Linux user who compiles C/CUDA software from source, can run shell diagnostics, inspect compiler commands, clean builds, and test environment variables.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed and cooperative; pastes complete commands and logs, answers version questions directly, reports both positive and negative outcomes, and clearly confirms when the correction works.
